newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand probing non-finance units of finance cos.
newsitem.headline: Thailand probing non-finance units of finance cos.

text.p: The Bank of Thailand (BOT) will investigate non-finance units of finance firms to see if any of them might have taken loans from their parents without giving sufficient collateral, a BOT official said on Thursday.
"Some are also suspected of having used funds for inappropriate purposes," said a BOT official who asked not to be identified. He did not define what the term "inappropriate purposes" meant.
The Bank of Thailand is currently empowered to only supervise and investigate financial institutions but not their non-finance affiliates.

Earlier this month, Thai authorities launched a massive revamp of the nation's troubled finance sector. They ordered 10 weakened finance firms to boost capital and told all financial institutions to raise provisioning for sub-standard loans.

Thai financial institutions are believed by analysts to have loaned over 800 billion baht ($30.8 billion) to the depressed property sector and a large portion of the loans are thought to be non-performing.
The central bank official said that among those to be investigated would be One Holding Plc, an investment arm of Thailand's largest finance firm Finance One Plc.
Liquidity problems faced by One Holding partly affected Finance One's financial health, the official said.
One Holding, which is listed under the textile sector, earlier this week said it had defaulted on $13.5 million due on its bill of exchange payment because of a liquidity problem.
